source: Minchat Shai on Gen 36:39 ('הדר — this one alone written with RESH, and every other הדד with dalet; so the Ramah, the Radak (in Chronicles it is with dalet, in the Torah with resh), and the Masorah with its sign')
claim_en: THE LAST KING'S RESH: the eighth and final Edomite king is written הדר with a RESH (36:39) — one of a kind against the dalet of his ancestor-kings (הדד at 36:35 and 36:36, builder-checked) and against his own name's dalet-spelling in Chronicles (named): the closing king's name shifted one letter into the Torah's own splendor-word.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 36:30 ('the Ramah's full ledger of the seven Seir-son writes: the FIRST full of vav and lean of yod; the third and the sixth lean of lean; the second, fourth, fifth, and seventh full of yod — against the Hilleli/Yerushalmi wavering at the sixth')
claim_en: THE SEVEN-POSITION NAME LEDGER: the sons of Seir carry the Dishon/Dishan name SEVEN times in this chapter, and the Ramah rules each position's spelling one by one — first with vav and no yod, third and sixth doubly lean, the other four with yod. SNAPSHOT matches the ledger at ALL SEVEN positions (36:21 twice, 36:25, 36:26, 36:28, 36:30 twice — every write builder-checked): a seven-station spelling law landing whole.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 36:31 ('ואלה המלכים — because Jacob said MY LORD to Esau eight times, eight kings reigned in Edom before any king in Israel')
claim_en: THE EIGHT MY-LORDS AND THE EIGHT KINGS: Jacob calls Esau MY LORD exactly eight times across the meeting (32:5 through 33:15, all eight builder-checked) — and the Torah's reign-verb וימלך ('and he reigned') appears exactly EIGHT times in the whole Torah, all of them Edom's kings in this ledger (36:32-39): the Kitzur's measure — eight deferences, eight crowns before Israel's — landing count for count, and closing the eight-mem gift-verse of 32:15 (gen_55) into one three-station arithmetic.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 36:7 ('מגוריהם — full in most books and the old Toledo Masorah; the Ramah settles it: the Vayishlach and Vayigash tokens FULL, and the one lean is the covenant-verse of Vaera; so Minchat Kohen')
claim_en: THE SOJOURNING-WORD'S THREE: מגוריהם ('the land of their SOJOURNINGS could not bear them,' 36:7) stands three times in the Torah — full here and at Jacob's hundred-and-thirty-years answer to Pharaoh (47:9), and lean exactly once at the covenant-verse 'the land of their sojournings, in which they sojourned' (Exod 6:4, builder-checked): the Ramah's two-full-one-lean landing to the letter.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 36:5 + 36:14 ('יעיש — read יעוש') + Kitzur 36:14 ('written with yod: he gathered TEN nations to come against Israel at the Temple's destruction, and ten exiles were exiled by his hand')
claim_en: WRITTEN YEISH, READ YEUSH: Esau's son is twice written יעיש with a yod and read יעוש with a vav (36:5 and 36:14) — and SNAPSHOT carries BOTH at each site as a written/read token-pair (builder-checked), while the third mention (36:18) needs no pair and is written full as read: the Kitzur counts the written yod as the TEN nations he would gather against the Temple. The two-token instrument working exactly where the tradition splits the name.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 36:7 ('ולא יכלה — two in the Masorah: the land COULD NOT bear them, and she COULD NO longer hide him (Exod 2:3): the Presence rested on Jacob and idolatrous company could not be borne')
claim_en: THE LAND THAT COULD NOT BEAR: יכלה of 'the land of their sojournings COULD NOT bear them together' (36:7) is paired by the Masorah with the one other 'could not' of its shape — Moses' mother, who COULD no longer hide him (Exod 2:3); the skeleton's third Torah token is Ephron's different verb ('no man will WITHHOLD his tomb,' 23:6, distinguished by its own pointing, builder-checked): the land that cannot carry Esau beside Jacob, and the house that cannot hide the deliverer.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 36:2-43 (the ledger's rulings: אהליבמה ONE word always; בעל חנן TWO words written and read, one name — the Ramah; הימם lean of yod between its two mems — the Ramah, with a Zohar teaching; מרחבות lean first vav full second — Hilleli + the Ramah; רכושם FULL against the printer; יעלם the ayin with sheva alone; מגדיאל the dalet dageshed)
claim_en: THE LEDGER'S NAMES AS RULED: Oholibamah ONE fused word at all four sites; Baal-hanan TWO written-and-read words that are one name (the Ramah); הימם of the wilderness lean between its two mems; Rehoboth-of-the-river lean in its first vav, full in its second; רכושם ('their property') FULL against the printer — the full form beside the lean רכשו class of Gen 14 and 31; יעלם with plain sheva on the ayin (a FOURTH guttural witness for the half-vowel boundary); and מגדיאל with its dalet dageshed — every ruling builder-checked in the stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 36:9 ('ואלה תלדות עשו אבי אדום — there is NO paragraph break there')
claim_en: NO BREAK AT THE SECOND HEADING (paragraph layer, uninstrumented): Minchat Shai rules that the ledger's second generations-heading — 'and these are the generations of Esau, father of Edom, in Mount Seir' (36:9) — opens NO new paragraph: Esau's two ledgers run as one skin. The paragraph layer is absent from SNAPSHOT's stream; filed with the Vayetze-head and wheat-harvest members.

THE PENALTY MINTED AT GEN_55 IS COUNTED HERE, AND BOTH NUMBERS ARE EIGHT. The chain sets Edom's eight named kings against Israel's eight - naming both lists - and states the alternation rule: when one crowns kings the other appoints judges, chieftains against princes, until a later empire scrambles both. Machine-checked in our own ink: the deference at gen_55 stands exactly eight times across Genesis 32-33, and 36:32-39 records exactly eight reigns before any king of Israel. A numeric claim spoken in one block and counted in another, with both ends derived in the same sitting.

check.note: A penalty count minted at an earlier block and discharged here, both ends verified against the corpus in one sitting.

claim_en: THE KING-LIST IS READ CONSTITUTIONALLY, AS A SHIP OF IMPORTED PARTS. Their kings come from elsewhere - one from one town, one from a river-city - mast from one place and anchors from another: no dynasty and no soil. The estate seized hastily at the start is read as these kings who reigned before Israel had any, and its end left unblessed. A genealogy read as a claim about the legitimacy structure of a state rather than as a list.

check.note: A king-list read as evidence about a state's constitutional structure - imported rulers, no dynastic succession.

claim_en: THE GENEALOGY IS READ AS A DELIBERATE EXPOSURE, AND ITS COUNT IS DISPUTED. The roster is peeled like an onion - I have exposed his hidden places - specifically to expose the illegitimate births among them, with the number disputed at three against four, and one name identified as such because it appears in two incompatible lines. A standing credit adds a second exhibit, one figure listed both as brother and as son of the same man. The chain treats a list of names as an evidentiary document and audits it for internal contradiction.

check.note: A genealogy audited as evidence for illegitimacy, the count disputed, with names appearing in incompatible lines as proof.

claim_en: A DEPARTURE IS READ AS EVASION OF A RECORDED DEBT. He went to another land DUE TO his brother - and R. Eliezer reads the cause as the promissory note: he left the Land to escape the servitude clause of the covenant, the four hundred years his descendants would otherwise owe. A migration verse turned into a claim about who bears an obligation the text recorded four blocks earlier.

check.note: A migration read as escaping a covenantal debt recorded in an earlier block, shifting who bears the obligation.

claim_en: SUPPLIER LIABILITY IS APPLIED TO A STATE. I will contend only with the city that supplied the king - the rule being that the supplier of a ruler is liable for him, carried by a parable about who sustains whom, and seated on the one king in the list whose town is named as his origin. A commercial liability principle transposed to the relations between polities.

check.note: A supplier-liability principle applied to a city that furnished a king, transposing commercial liability to statecraft.

claim_en: THE LAST NAMES IN THE LIST ARE READ AS A COUNTDOWN AND AN ESCROW. One name is decoded as the day a particular emperor took the throne, with the report of a dream stating that ONE MORE KING is required for Edom; another is read as destined to PILE TREASURES for the messianic king. The final entries of a genealogy are treated as a schedule with a remaining count and as assets held in escrow rather than as names.

check.note: The closing names of a genealogy read as a remaining-count schedule and as treasuries held in escrow.

claim_en: A NAME CARRYING A FORGIVENESS CLAIM IS QUIETLY REPLACED IN THE LEDGER. The bride at 28:9 was read as named for the forgiveness of the groom's iniquities; in this roster the same woman appears under a different name. The chain records the shift rather than harmonizing it, so a claim built on a name is left standing against a list that does not carry the name.

check.note: A doctrinal claim built on a name left standing against a later roster that records a different name for the same person.

claim_en: THE TRANSLATION CASTS AN INDEPENDENT THIRD VOTE ON A FAMOUS OBSCURE WORD. What was found in the wilderness is disputed in the tradition between mules and hot springs; Onkelos renders THE MIGHTY ONES - giants. A third reading of a word that appears once, entered by the translation without argument, and the clearest instance in this sweep of the buffer holding a lexical seat of its own rather than voting in someone else's dispute.

check.note: A translation supplying a third independent reading of a disputed hapax rather than choosing between existing options.
